title: Icecream Fitness FAQ review
summary: He goes through the Ice Cream Fitness FAQ, criticising its defensive tone and 'never change the program' stance, and mocks the author along the way. Topics include box squats for bad knees, deadlift 'CNS fatigue', the idea that no lift is essential, retake-then-deload-10% plateau handling, accessories for novices, and hyperextension versus good morning substitutions.
claims: Program FAQs are usually written to defend the program because authors think they invented fire, not to help people get the most from it
Writing a program like Ice Cream Fitness is easy: a few compound movements and random schemes like 5x5

People avoid the program not because 1.5 hours is long but because squats, deadlifts, overhead press and rows at high intensity on the same day with no rep variation is too much; 1.5 hours is still a bit long for novices
The author calling trainees lazy or cowards for not following his program is hypocritical
You stop being a novice not when you bench two plates but when you can write effective programs for yourself
There is no such thing as a proven program; most famous novice programs are famous because they are old, dating from the start of YouTube fitness, not because they are good
If changing one thing breaks a program it is a bad program; forbidding novices from changing anything is ego
With bad knees, fix the knees rather than switching to box squats; a wide box squat becomes a good-morning-like hip hinge that no longer trains the quads
Box squats are a good way to rehab patellar tendinitis with low weight, but loading them like normal squats aggravates shearing forces on the knee
The bottom of the squat, where you reverse the bar, is the hardest part; a box makes it easier, less draining and less taxing on the cardiovascular system
Squats cause more fatigue than deadlifts; what people call deadlift CNS fatigue is usually lower back strain from pulling with the back instead of hamstrings and glutes
One set of 5 is enough for deadlifts, not because more is dangerous but because you do not need more
Heavy high-rep squats like widowmakers are brutal on the cardiovascular system and muscular endurance and very painful
No lift is essential: a novice who dislikes squats or deadlifts can use another knee flexion or hip hinge; novice programs wrongly groom everyone into powerlifters
Lateral raises and face pulls cannot replace each other; one loads the medial delt, the other the rear delt, so do both
He does not have much experience lifting on a cut so avoids giving advice on it
Diet is overhyped for people who already know how to control calories; he partly agrees that cardio is unnecessary
Retaking a failed weight and then cutting 10% does not teach plateau handling; lifters end up stuck repeating it, when they should change volume and intensity and introduce new rep ranges
Accessory work is fine for novices and prevents a backlog of side projects later; an accessory is whatever complements what the training misses

Good mornings are not a substitute for hyperextensions: good mornings are a squat accessory with a better stretch, hyperextensions a deadlift accessory that is healthier on the lower back with a better hamstring contraction
Rest 3-5 minutes between strength sets and 1-2 minutes between volume accessory sets
exercises: useful for patellar tendinitis rehab; wide heavy version becomes a hip hinge
lower back pain comes from poor form
medial delt; not replaceable by face pulls
deadlift accessory, healthier on lower back, hamstring contraction
